title: Palak Paneer Spinach Cottage Cheese

seo.imageAlt: A bowl of authentic Indian Palak Paneer with spinach and cottage cheese, garnished with cream and cilantro, served with naan bread.
seo.imageCaption: Enjoy this vibrant and creamy Palak Paneer, a classic Indian vegetarian dish that's surprisingly easy to make at home!

description: Palak Paneer is a quintessential Indian vegetarian delight, featuring tender cubes of fresh paneer (Indian cottage cheese) simmered in a vibrant, creamy spinach gravy. This wholesome and flavorful dish is subtly spiced, offering a perfect balance of earthy greens and rich dairy, making it a beloved staple across India.

instructions.title: Blanch the Spinach
instructions.text: Boil water in a large pot. Add spinach and blanch for 2-3 minutes until wilted. Immediately transfer to an ice bath to retain color. Drain well and blend into a smooth puree.

instructions.title: Prepare the Paneer
instructions.text: Heat 1 tablespoon of ghee or oil in a pan. Lightly fry the paneer cubes until golden brown on all sides. Remove and set aside. Alternatively, you can simply add them raw if you prefer softer paneer.

instructions.title: Sauté Aromatics
instructions.text: In the same pan, add the remaining ghee or oil. Add cumin seeds and let them splutter. Then add finely chopped onions and sauté until translucent and light golden brown.

instructions.title: Build the Gravy Base
instructions.text: Add ginger garlic paste and green chilies. Sauté for 1-2 minutes until fragrant. Add tomato puree and cook, stirring occasionally, until the oil separates from the mixture, indicating it's well cooked.

instructions.title: Add Spices and Spinach
instructions.text: Stir in turmeric powder, coriander powder, and red chili powder. Cook for a minute, ensuring the spices are fragrant. Then add the spinach puree, mix well, and bring to a gentle simmer. Add a little water if the gravy is too thick. Season with salt to taste.

instructions.title: Combine and Finish
instructions.text: Add the prepared paneer cubes to the simmering spinach gravy. Stir gently and cook for 5-7 minutes, allowing the paneer to absorb the rich flavors. Stir in garam masala. Garnish with a swirl of fresh cream and serve hot with naan or rice.

tips: To retain the vibrant green color of spinach, always blanch it briefly and then immediately shock it in ice-cold water before pureeing.
For extra flavor and texture, lightly fry the paneer cubes until golden. If you prefer softer paneer, you can soak the fried paneer in warm water for 10 minutes before adding to the gravy.
Adjust the spice levels according to your preference. A pinch of sugar can help balance the tanginess of tomatoes and enhance the overall flavor profile of the dish.
